name: ASP.NET
tagline: The enterprise-grade back-end command station of .NET.
timeTravelLog: Released by Microsoft in 2002, ASP.NET Core is the modern, cross-platform successor — rewritten from the ground up in 2016 for Linux, macOS, and Windows with blazing performance topping the TechEmpower benchmarks.
overview: ASP.NET Core is Microsoft's open-source, cross-platform web framework for building modern web applications and APIs with C#. It provides Razor Pages, MVC architecture, Minimal APIs, built-in dependency injection, Entity Framework Core ORM, and first-class cloud deployment support.

syllabus.title: Module 1: ASP.NET Core Architecture & Project Setup
syllabus.desc: Understanding the program entry point, middleware pipeline, and DI container.
syllabus.content: Every ASP.NET Core app starts in Program.cs. WebApplication.CreateBuilder() sets up the host. Services are registered in the DI container (builder.Services.Add*). The app.Use* calls build the middleware pipeline — a chain of request-processing functions. app.Run() starts the Kestrel web server.
syllabus.interactiveTip: The order of middleware matters! UseAuthentication() must always come before UseAuthorization() in the pipeline. Reversing this is a common beginner mistake that silently breaks auth!

syllabus.title: Module 2: Controllers & Routing (MVC Architecture)
syllabus.desc: Building HTTP endpoints with attribute routing in the MVC controller model.
syllabus.content: ASP.NET Core MVC routes HTTP requests to Controller action methods based on route templates. [ApiController] enables automatic model validation and response formatting. [HttpGet], [HttpPost], [HttpPut], [HttpDelete] attribute decorators define HTTP verbs. Route parameters are bound from URL segments, query strings, or request bodies automatically.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Use CreatedAtAction() for POST responses instead of Ok() — it returns HTTP 201 with a Location header pointing to the new resource URL. This follows REST conventions properly!

syllabus.title: Module 3: Entity Framework Core (ORM & Migrations)
syllabus.desc: Querying and persisting data to databases using code-first Entity Framework ORM.
syllabus.content: Entity Framework Core is .NET's ORM — it maps C# classes to database tables. DbContext represents the database connection and set of tables. LINQ queries are translated to SQL automatically. Code-first migrations generate and track schema changes in version control. Add-Migration creates migration files. Update-Database applies them to the database.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Never use .ToList() when you can use .ToListAsync() — all EF Core database operations should be awaited async to prevent thread blocking under concurrent load!

syllabus.title: Module 4: Authentication & JWT Authorization
syllabus.desc: Securing API endpoints with JWT bearer token authentication.
syllabus.content: ASP.NET Core's authentication middleware validates JWT tokens on every protected request. The JWT is generated on login using JwtSecurityTokenHandler with claims (user ID, roles) signed by a secret key. [Authorize] attribute protects entire controllers or specific actions. [AllowAnonymous] explicitly bypasses auth for login and register endpoints.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Store the JWT secret in appsettings.json only for development. For production, use Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, or environment variables — never commit secrets to git repositories!

syllabus.title: Module 5: Minimal APIs (Streamlined Endpoint Design)
syllabus.desc: Building lightweight HTTP APIs with minimal boilerplate using .NET 6+ Minimal API syntax.
syllabus.content: Minimal APIs reduce ceremony for simple endpoints — no controllers, no [HttpGet] attributes, no class definitions. Route handlers are registered directly in Program.cs using app.MapGet(), app.MapPost(), etc. They support dependency injection, async handlers, model binding, and middleware — with far less code than traditional MVC.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Use Results.Ok(), Results.NotFound(), Results.Created(), and Results.Problem() instead of raw returns in Minimal APIs — they produce properly typed HTTP responses with correct status codes!

syllabus.title: Module 6: Middleware Pipeline & Error Handling
syllabus.desc: Building custom middleware and global error handling for production-grade APIs.
syllabus.content: Middleware are C# classes that handle HTTP requests and responses in the pipeline. Custom middleware wraps requests with logging, exception catching, rate limiting, or request transformation. Global exception handling via exception middleware prevents raw stack traces from leaking to API consumers — always return RFC 7807 ProblemDetails for consistent error responses.
syllabus.interactiveTip: Register error handling middleware as the FIRST middleware in the pipeline (before UseHttpsRedirection) so it can catch exceptions thrown anywhere in the pipeline below it!

syllabus.title: Module 7: Deployment to Azure & Docker
syllabus.desc: Containerizing and deploying ASP.NET Core applications to the cloud.
syllabus.content: ASP.NET Core apps can be deployed as standalone executables, IIS-hosted applications, Docker containers, or serverless Azure Functions. A multi-stage Dockerfile builds the app in a full SDK image and then copies only the published output to a lightweight runtime image, dramatically reducing container size.
syllabus.codeExample:
# Multi-stage Dockerfile
# Stage 1: Build
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY . .
RUN dotnet restore
RUN dotnet publish -c Release -o /app/publish

# Stage 2: Runtime (small image)
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0 AS runtime
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/publish .
EXPOSE 8080
ENV ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://+:8080
ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "MissionControl.dll"]

# Build and run
# docker build -t mission-control .
# docker run -p 8080:8080 mission-control
syllabus.interactiveTip: Use multi-stage Docker builds — the SDK image is ~700MB but the runtime image is only ~200MB. Your final production container should contain ONLY the published output, not the build toolchain!

quiz.question: What is the primary role of WebApplication.CreateBuilder() in ASP.NET Core?
options: Sets up the host, configures the DI container, and loads application settings
Compiles the C# code to machine code
Creates a Docker container for the app
quiz.explanation: WebApplication.CreateBuilder() initializes the application host — loading configuration from appsettings.json and environment variables, setting up the DI container, and configuring the logging infrastructure.

quiz.question: What does the [Authorize] attribute do in ASP.NET Core?
options: Logs all requests to the decorated endpoint
Restricts access to authenticated (and optionally role-authorized) users only
Generates Swagger documentation for the endpoint
quiz.explanation: [Authorize] causes ASP.NET Core's authorization middleware to reject unauthenticated requests with HTTP 401. Role-based restrictions can be added with [Authorize(Roles = "Admin")] for HTTP 403 on role mismatch.

quiz.question: In EF Core, what command generates a migration from model changes?
quiz.explanation: 'dotnet ef migrations add MigrationName' generates a migration file representing the diff between your current C# models and the last migration. 'dotnet ef database update' then applies it to the database.

quest.title: Quest: Build a Mission Tracker REST API
quest.challenge: Create a full ASP.NET Core REST API for mission management with full CRUD operations.
instructions: 1. Create a Mission entity with Id, Name, Status, and CreatedAt fields.
2. Set up DbContext with SQLite (simple for local dev) and run an initial migration.
3. Build a MissionsController with GET (all), GET (by id), POST, PUT, and DELETE endpoints.
4. Add JWT authentication — protect POST/PUT/DELETE behind [Authorize].
5. Add a global error handling middleware that catches unhandled exceptions and returns a ProblemDetails JSON response.
